evergreen.title: Fed Policy Path (market-implied)
evergreen.text: The 2-year Treasury yield (4.89%) is 101bp above the effective fed funds rate (3.88%): above the policy rate, meaning markets are pricing higher-for-longer or further hikes — bearish. Target range: 3.75%–4.00%.

evergreen.title: US Real Yields (10Y TIPS)
evergreen.text: 10Y real yield is 2.91%, up 47bp over 4 weeks (as of 2026-09-29): rising real yields raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold — bearish. Real yields are the most direct macro driver of gold.

evergreen.title: US Dollar Trend (Fed Broad Index)
evergreen.text: The Fed's broad trade-weighted dollar index is 120.3, up 1.3% over 4 weeks (as of 2026-09-25): a firmer dollar makes gold pricier for foreign buyers — bearish.

evergreen.title: Central Bank Gold Buying (Structural Trend)
evergreen.text: Central banks globally have been net buyers of gold for several consecutive years, diversifying reserves away from the dollar. A slow-moving structural tailwind; check World Gold Council quarterly data for the latest.

evergreen.title: US Fiscal Deficit / Debt Trajectory
evergreen.text: Elevated US debt and deficit levels support structural demand for gold as a reserve-diversification and currency-debasement hedge.

evergreen.title: Geopolitical Risk Premium
evergreen.text: Ongoing geopolitical stress supports a baseline safe-haven bid under gold. Acute escalations or de-escalations show up as live items below.
